summary: Modular Curves Part II, part R13.3 (stages R13.3–R14.2), checkpoint 1, in 10 nodes. R14.1 and R14.2 are planned at declaration level from Conrad's appendix to Ribet–Stein: the Hecke correspondence X₁(N, p) ⇉ X₁(N), diamond and Atkin–Lehner operators, their composition relations, J₁(N) with Picard/Albanese functoriality, the Hecke operators on J₁(N) extended over ℤ[1/N], the integral Hecke algebra, Weil-pairing adjointness and the Tate module. R13.3–R13.6 are not yet planned. RS-06 (accepted) narrows R14.1 and R14.2; this checkpoint follows its keeps, importing isogenies from Tau Ceti ModularCurves §2B and the Jacobian scheme from JacobianChallenge layer D, and comparing with ModularForms layers 2 and 8.

nodes.title: The degeneracy maps π₁, π₂ : X₁(N, p) → X₁(N) and the Hecke correspondence T_p
nodes.statement: Fix N ≥ 5 and a prime p. Over ℤ[1/Np], Y₁(N, p) is the base of the universal triple (E, P, C): E an elliptic curve, P a point of exact order N, C ⊂ E a finite locally free subgroup scheme of order p, not contained in the subgroup generated by P on geometric fibres when p | N. X₁(N, p) is its compactification, proper smooth over ℤ[1/Np] and finite flat over ℙ¹. The degeneracy maps are π₁^{(p)}(E, P, C) = (E, P) and π₂^{(p)}(E, P, C) = (E/C, P mod C) from Y₁(N, p) to Y₁(N)[1/p]. They extend uniquely to finite flat maps X₁(N, p) → X₁(N)[1/p], of degree p + 1 if p ∤ N and p if p | N. The Hecke correspondence T_p is the pair (π₁^{(p)}, π₂^{(p)}), i.e. X₁(N, p) → X₁(N) ×_{ℤ[1/Np]} X₁(N).
hypotheses: N ≥ 5, as in the source, where X₁(N) is a proper smooth ℤ[1/N]-scheme with a universal object over Y₁(N) (S₂(Γ₁(N)) = 0 for N < 5). The curves X₁(N), X₁(N, p) with their geometrically connected fibres are ModularCurvesPartII R13.2; this node builds the maps.
When p | N the disjointness of C from ⟨P⟩ is needed for π₂ to make sense: otherwise P mod C has order N/p.

π₂ does not preserve the fibration over 𝔸¹ given by the j-line coordinates of the two moduli problems. Its extension to the compactifications uses minimal regular proper models of curves over a Dedekind base, not the moduli interpretation at the cusps.
The quotient E/C and the isogeny E → E/C are imported from Tau Ceti ModularCurves §2B (isogenies and quotients) and AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A3, as RS-06 directs.

Degree counts: for p ∤ N the fibre of π₁ over (E, P) is the set of the p + 1 subgroups of order p of E[p] ≅ (ℤ/p)² over an algebraically closed field of characteristic ≠ p. For p | N, the one subgroup meeting ⟨P⟩ is excluded, leaving p.

proofSteps: Representability of Y₁(N, p) and its compactification: R13.2 (request). This source cites Deligne–Rapoport and Katz–Mazur for it.

π₁ is forgetful. π₂ uses the quotient E/C by a finite locally free subgroup, an elliptic curve with an isogeny E → E/C of degree p (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A3). P mod C has exact order N by the disjointness condition (automatic when p ∤ N).

Extension to X₁(N, p) → X₁(N)[1/p]: the maps are defined on the dense open Y₁(N, p), and the source extends them using the theory of minimal regular proper models of curves over a Dedekind base (R13.4). Finiteness and flatness hold because a non-constant map of proper smooth curves with geometrically connected fibres is finite flat.
Degrees: count geometric points in a general fibre, as in the hypotheses.
acceptance: N = 11, p = 2: deg π₁ = 3 (three subgroups of order 2 in E[2]).
N = 10, p = 5: deg π₁ = 5; of the six subgroups of order 5 in E[5], the one containing 2P is excluded.
Analytically π₁ is induced by z ↦ z on 𝔥, for the uniformisations (ℂ/[1, z], 1/N, ⟨1/p⟩) of Y₁(N, p) (p ∤ N) and (ℂ/[1, z], 1/N) of Y₁(N).

nodes.title: Diamond operators I_n on X₁(N) and X₁(N, p)
nodes.statement: For n ∈ (ℤ/Nℤ)^×, I_n : Y₁(N) → Y₁(N) over ℤ[1/N] is (E, P) ↦ (E, nP), and on Y₁(N, p) it is (E, P, C) ↦ (E, nP, C). They extend to automorphisms of X₁(N) over ℤ[1/N] and of X₁(N, p) over ℤ[1/Np]. They satisfy I_n I_m = I_{nm} and I_{−1} = id, so they give an action of (ℤ/Nℤ)^×/{±1}. They commute with the degeneracy maps: π_i^{(p)} ∘ I_n = I_n ∘ π_i^{(p)}.
hypotheses: n must be a unit mod N: otherwise nP does not have exact order N.
I_{−1} = id because [−1] : E ≅ E carries (E, P) to (E, −P); so only ±n matter.
Analytically I_n is induced by any γ_n ∈ SL₂(ℤ) with γ_n ≡ (n^{−1} *; 0 n) mod N.

tests.name: TauCeti.ModularCurves.not_diamond_nonunit
tests.statement: For n not prime to N, (E, nP) is not a point of X₁(N): nP does not have exact order N.

proofSteps: Moduli: (E, P) ↦ (E, nP) preserves the moduli problem, and I_n I_m = I_{nm} is immediate.
I_{−1}: the automorphism [−1] of E is an isomorphism (E, P) ≅ (E, −P).
Extension: as for the degeneracy maps (node degeneracy-maps-and-hecke-correspondence). An automorphism of Y₁(N) extends to X₁(N).
Commutation with π₂: (E/C, nP mod C) = (E/C, n(P mod C)).
acceptance: N = 11: (ℤ/11)^×/{±1} has order 5, and the diamond operators generate a cyclic group of order 5 acting on X₁(11).
Analytically γ_n acts on 𝔥 and induces I_n; on q-expansions it is the classical ⟨n⟩ (via R14.3's Shimura isomorphism).

nodes.title: The Atkin–Lehner operator w_ζ on X₁(N) over ℤ[1/N, ζ_N]
nodes.statement: For a primitive N-th root of unity ζ, w_ζ : Y₁(N) → Y₁(N) over ℤ[1/N, ζ_N] is (E, P) ↦ (E/⟨P⟩, P′). Here ⟨P⟩ is the étale subgroup of order N generated by P, and P′ ∈ (E[N]/⟨P⟩)(S) is determined by ⟨P, P′⟩_N = ζ for the Weil pairing (any lift of P′ to E[N]). It extends to X₁(N). It satisfies w_{ζ^j} ∘ w_ζ = I_j for j ∈ (ℤ/Nℤ)^×; in particular w_ζ² = id. Since w_ζ = w_{ζ^{−1}}, w_ζ descends to ℤ[1/N, ζ_N]^+. Over ℂ, with ζ = e^{2πi/N}, it is w_N : z ↦ −1/(Nz) for the sign convention ⟨1/N, z/N⟩_N = e^{2πi/N} on ℂ/[1, z].
hypotheses: The Weil pairing sign convention is that of Katz–Mazur and Mumford, opposite to Silverman's. With the other convention w_{e^{2πi/N}} becomes w_N composed with a diamond operator.
w_ζ is not defined over ℤ[1/N]: g ∈ G_ℚ carries w_ζ to w_{g(ζ)}.
w_ζ = w_{ζ^{−1}} because (E, P) ≅ (E, −P) via [−1].

tests.name: TauCeti.ModularCurves.atkinLehner_comp_diamond
tests.statement: w_{ζ^j} ∘ w_ζ = I_j, so conjugation by w_ζ inverts the diamond action.

proofSteps: Well-definedness: E[N]/⟨P⟩ is étale cyclic of order N, and the Weil pairing gives E[N]/⟨P⟩ ≅ μ_N ⊗ Hom(⟨P⟩, ℤ/N). So there is a unique P′ with ⟨P, P′⟩ = ζ, and its image in E/⟨P⟩ has exact order N.
w_{ζ^j} w_ζ = I_j: apply the construction twice. The dual isogeny identifies (E/⟨P⟩)/⟨P′⟩ with E, carrying the second P′ to a multiple of P fixed by the two pairings.
Descent to ℤ[1/N, ζ_N]^+: w_ζ = w_{ζ^{−1}} and étale descent along ℤ[1/N, ζ_N]^+ → ℤ[1/N, ζ_N].
Extension to X₁(N): as for the other operators.
acceptance: Over ℂ with ζ = e^{2πi/N}: (ℂ/[1, z], 1/N) ↦ (ℂ/[1/N, z], z/N), since ⟨1/N, z/N⟩ = e^{2πi/N}. Multiplying by N gives (ℂ/[1, Nz], z), and multiplying by −1/(Nz) gives (ℂ/[1, −1/(Nz)], −1/N) ≅ (ℂ/[1, −1/(Nz)], 1/N). This is the point −1/(Nz), the source's identification w_{e^{2πi/N}} = w_N.
w_ζ² = id is the case j = 1 of w_{ζ^j} w_ζ = I_j.

nodes.title: Composition relations among the Hecke correspondences, diamond and Atkin–Lehner operators
nodes.statement: On X₁(N) over the relevant bases: (i) I_n ∘ I_m = I_{nm} and I_n commutes with every π_i^{(p)}; (ii) for primes p ≠ q, X₁(N, p) ×_{π₂,X₁(N),π₁} X₁(N, q) ≅ X₁(N, pq) ≅ X₁(N, q) ×_{π₂,X₁(N),π₁} X₁(N, p) over ℤ[1/Npq], compatibly with the outer degeneracy maps, so the correspondences T_p and T_q commute; (iii) w_{ζ^j} ∘ w_ζ = I_j.
hypotheses: X₁(N, pq) parametrises (E, P, C) with C cyclic of order pq meeting ⟨P⟩ trivially; for p ≠ q, C = C_p ⊕ C_q uniquely.

How w_ζ interacts with π₁, π₂ holds only up to a diamond operator (it realises w_N T_p w_N as the adjoint of T_p). The source states that relation on the Jacobian, where it is node weil-pairing-adjointness. It is not asserted here on the moduli side.
The double-coset formula T_p ↔ Γ₁(N) diag(1, p) Γ₁(N) is the analytic side, compared in R14.3; it is not re-proved here.
proofSteps: (i): moduli, node diamond-operators.

(ii): a point of the fibre product is (E, P, C_p) together with (E/C_p, P, C′_q), C′_q ⊂ E/C_p of order q. Its preimage C_q ⊂ E has order q (p ≠ q) and C_p ⊕ C_q is cyclic of order pq. Conversely (E, P, C) with C cyclic of order pq splits uniquely. Both composites send (E, P, C) to (E, P) and (E/C, P mod C).
(iii): moduli computation with the Weil pairing (node atkin-lehner-involution).
acceptance: N = 11, p = 2, q = 3: X₁(11, 6) is a fibre product of degree 3·4 = 12 = (2 + 1)(3 + 1) over X₁(11) through either order, as the degrees of the degeneracy maps multiply.
p = q is excluded: X₁(N, p) ×_{X₁(N)} X₁(N, p) contains the component where C′ is the image of E[p], which gives the relation T_p² = T_{p²} + p⟨p⟩ rather than a cyclic subgroup of order p².

sources.match: Commutativity of the Hecke operators; this node gives its moduli form.

nodes.title: Over ℂ the algebraic correspondences are the classical Hecke, diamond and Atkin–Lehner operators
nodes.statement: Under (X₁(N) ×_{ℤ[1/N]} ℂ)^an ≅ Γ₁(N)\𝔥 ∪ {cusps}, identifying (ℂ/[1, z], 1/N) with the class of z: π₁^{(p)} is induced by z ↦ z, I_n by any γ_n ∈ SL₂(ℤ) with γ_n ≡ (n^{−1} *; 0 n) mod N, and w_{e^{2πi/N}} by z ↦ −1/(Nz). On H⁰(X₁(N)^an, Ω¹) = S₂(Γ₁(N), ℂ), the pullback–trace (π₁^{(p)})_* ∘ (π₂^{(p)})^* is the classical T_p, the unique double-coset operator Γ₁(N) diag(1, p) Γ₁(N) of Tau Ceti ModularForms layer 2, and I_n^* is ⟨n⟩.
hypotheses: The trace (π₁)_* is weighted by ramification indices, (a_y) ↦ Σ e_y a_y on stalks. A naive average over fibres would be wrong at the elliptic points and cusps.

The Betti form of the same comparison, on H¹(X₁(N)^an, ℤ), is ModularCurvesPartII:R14.3/weight-two-shimura-isomorphism (Conrad's Theorem 5.1). This node is its holomorphic part, which RS-06 assigns to R14.1.
The comparison of X₁(N)^an with the analytic quotient is R12.6; its proof needs care with the relative theory of elliptic curves over analytic bases.
proofSteps: The uniformisations of Y₁(N)^an and Y₁(N, p)^an by (ℂ/[1, z], 1/N) and (ℂ/[1, z], 1/N, ⟨1/p⟩) (p ∤ N) or ⟨z/p⟩ (p | N) identify π₁ with z ↦ z. The moduli formulas identify I_n with γ_n and w_ζ with z ↦ −1/(Nz) (node atkin-lehner-involution).
Conrad's Theorem 5.1 identifies T_p ⊕ T̄_p with (π₁)_* (π₂)^* on H¹ ⊗ ℂ; restricting to H⁰(Ω¹) gives the classical T_p on S₂(Γ₁(N), ℂ).

Uniqueness of the double-coset normalisation: T_p on S₂ is the operator of Γ₁(N) diag(1, p) Γ₁(N) in the normalisation of Tau Ceti ModularForms layer 2 (request), and Tau Ceti's abstract T(m) satisfies T(m)T(n) = T(mn) for coprime m, n.
acceptance: N = 11, p = 2: (π₁)_*(π₂)^* acts on S₂(Γ₁(11)) = ℂ·f (f = 11a) by a_2 = −2.
w₁₁ acts on f = 11a by its Atkin–Lehner eigenvalue −1: for p ∥ N a newform with trivial character has a_p = −ε_p, and a₁₁(11a) = 1.

nodes.title: The modular Jacobian J₁(N) = Pic⁰_{X₁(N)/ℤ[1/N]} and Picard/Albanese functoriality for finite maps of curves
nodes.statement: For N ≥ 5, J₁(N) := Pic⁰_{X₁(N)/ℤ[1/N]} is an abelian scheme over ℤ[1/N] with a canonical principal polarisation, and it is the Néron model of its generic fibre. For a finite flat map f : X → Y of proper smooth curves with geometrically connected fibres over a base S, there are f^* = Pic⁰(f) : Pic⁰_Y → Pic⁰_X and f_* = Alb(f) : Pic⁰_X → Pic⁰_Y, with f_* ∘ f^* = deg f, and f^* and f_* are dual under the canonical principal polarisations. Over ℂ they are the maps induced on H¹(·, 𝒪)/H¹(·, ℤ) by pullback and trace. The same applies to J₀(N) = Pic⁰ of the coarse curve X₀(N) over ℤ[1/N].
hypotheses: Pic⁰ of a proper smooth curve with geometrically connected fibres over any base is an abelian scheme (Grothendieck), and an abelian scheme over a Dedekind base is the Néron model of its generic fibre.
J₀(N) needs X₀(N) proper smooth over ℤ[1/N] as a coarse space (R13.4a).
Over ℂ, the tangent-space identification from the exponential sequence is −2πi times the algebraic one (source's warning); this affects no Hecke statement.

proofSteps: Representability of the relative Picard functor and the Jacobian scheme: Tau Ceti JacobianChallenge layer D; its abelian-scheme structure and polarisation: AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A6 (requests, as RS-06 directs).
Néron property: NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties R11.1/R11.4 (request).
Albanese functoriality: Pic⁰(f) is the pullback of line bundles; Alb(f) is the norm of line bundles (or its dual under the autodualities); f_* f^* = deg f is the norm of a pullback.
Duality of f^* and f_*: Conrad's Lemma 5.4 analytically; algebraically, the autoduality of Jacobians identifies Pic⁰(f)^∨ with Alb(f).
acceptance: N = 11: X₁(11) has genus 1, so J₁(11) is an elliptic curve over ℤ[1/11], isogenous to X₀(11).

nodes.title: The Hecke operators T_p^*, (T_p)_*, ⟨n⟩^*, ⟨n⟩_* and w_ζ on J₁(N), extended over ℤ[1/N]
nodes.statement: On J₁(N)[1/p] over ℤ[1/Np] define T_p^* = Alb(π₁^{(p)}) ∘ Pic⁰(π₂^{(p)}) and (T_p)_* = Alb(π₂^{(p)}) ∘ Pic⁰(π₁^{(p)}). On J₁(N) over ℤ[1/N] define ⟨n⟩^* = Pic⁰(I_n) and ⟨n⟩_* = Alb(I_n). On J₁(N) over ℤ[1/N, ζ_N] define w_ζ = Pic⁰(w_ζ) = Alb(w_ζ). By the Néron mapping property, T_p^* and (T_p)_* extend uniquely to endomorphisms of J₁(N) over ℤ[1/N], so they are defined on J₁(N)_{𝔽_p} for p ∤ N. ⟨n⟩_* = ⟨n^{−1}⟩^*. Over ℂ, the (·)^* operators are those of Conrad's Definition 5.5 and the (·)_* operators those of Definition 5.6.
hypotheses: The extension over ℤ[1/N] needs the Néron property: π₂^{(p)} is not defined over ℤ[1/N] from what precedes, so T_p^* on J₁(N)_{𝔽_p} does not come from a correspondence on X₁(N)_{𝔽_p} without a further construction.
Under S₂(Γ₁(N), ℂ) ≅ Cot₀(J₁(N)_ℂ), the (·)^*-action of T is the Petersson adjoint of the classical T, while the (·)_*-action is the classical one (Conrad's warning before Definition 5.6).
⟨n⟩_* = ⟨n^{−1}⟩^* because I_n^{−1} = I_{n^{−1}} and Alb of an automorphism is Pic⁰ of its inverse.

nodes.title: The integral Hecke algebra T₁(N) ⊂ End(J₁(N)): finiteness, commutativity and faithfulness
nodes.statement: T₁(N)^* ⊂ End_{ℤ[1/N]}(J₁(N)) is the subring generated by the T_p^* (all p) and the ⟨n⟩^*, and T₁(N)_* the subring generated by the (T_p)_* and ⟨n⟩_*. Each is a commutative ring, finite free as a ℤ-module. It acts faithfully on the finite free ℤ-module H¹(X₁(N)^an, ℤ) and on the finite free ℤ_ℓ-module T_ℓ(J₁(N)). Over ℂ each is identified with the classical weight-two Hecke ring T₁(N) ⊂ End_ℤ(H¹(X₁(N)^an, ℤ)) generated by T_p^* and ⟨n⟩^*. The two are isomorphic (T ↦ its Rosati adjoint).
hypotheses: Finiteness comes from End(J₁(N)_ℚ) being a finite free ℤ-module, which holds for every abelian variety over a field.
Commutativity is inherited from the analytic Hecke ring (Conrad §5.1), or from node composition-relations-of-correspondences on the moduli side.

This is the integral Hecke algebra as a ring of endomorphisms of an actual finite module, as the stage requires. The version through modular symbols is Tau Ceti ModularForms layer 8; the two are compared through H¹(X₁(N)^an, ℤ).

proofSteps: Finite freeness: End(A) for an abelian variety A over a field is a finite free ℤ-module (Mumford), and J₁(N)_ℚ → J₁(N) induces End(J₁(N)) ≅ End(J₁(N)_ℚ) by the Néron property. A subring of a finite free ℤ-module is finite free.
Faithfulness on T_ℓ: End(A) → End(T_ℓ A) is injective (Tate). On H¹: via T_ℓ(J₁(N)_ℂ) ≅ H¹(X₁(N)^an, ℤ) ⊗ ℤ_ℓ (Conrad's (5.4)).
Identification with the classical ring: Conrad's Definition 5.5 and the faithfulness of the Tate-module functor on complex tori.
Adjoint isomorphism T₁(N)^* ≅ T₁(N)_*: node weil-pairing-adjointness.

Comparison with the modular-symbol Hecke algebra (RS-06): both act faithfully on lattices dual to each other inside H¹(X₁(N)^an, ℚ) (modular symbols are H₁ relative to the cusps), with the same T_p. So the two subrings of End(H¹ ⊗ ℚ) coincide, and so do their integral forms, being generated by the same operators.
acceptance: N = 11: T₁(11) is a subring of End(J₁(11)) = ℤ, hence T₁(11) = ℤ, with T_p acting by a_p(11a).
N = 23 (on J₀(23)): the Hecke algebra is ℤ[(1 + √5)/2], of rank 2 = dim J₀(23), matching K_f = ℚ(√5).

nodes.title: Weil-pairing adjoints on J₁(N): (·)^* and (·)_* are dual, and w_ζ exchanges them
nodes.statement: Let V_ℓ(N) = ℚ_ℓ ⊗ T_ℓ(J₁(N)) with its alternating Weil pairing (·,·)_ℓ from the canonical principal polarisation. For T ∈ T₁(N), the adjoint of T^* is T_*. For p ∤ N the adjoint of T_p (in either action) is ⟨p⟩^{−1}T_p, and that of ⟨n⟩ is ⟨n⟩^{−1}. w_ζ conjugates the (·)^*-action to the (·)_*-action, so with [x, y]_ℓ = (x, w_ζ y)_ℓ every T is self-adjoint. For g ∈ G_ℚ acting on ℚ̄-points, (g^{−1})^* ∘ w_{g(ζ)} ∘ g^* = w_ζ.
hypotheses: The Weil pairing and the cup product on H¹ differ by a sign (Conrad's Lemma 5.7), which does not affect adjoints.
The analytic counterpart with the cup product on H¹(X₁(N)^an, ℤ) is ModularCurvesPartII:R14.3/hecke-twisted-self-adjoint. This node is the Tate-module form used over 𝔽_p and ℚ.
proofSteps: Duality of Pic⁰(f) and Alb(f) (node jacobian-and-functoriality) gives (T_p^*)^† = (Alb(π₁)Pic⁰(π₂))^† = Alb(π₂)Pic⁰(π₁) = (T_p)_*, and similarly for ⟨n⟩.
Adjoint of T_p for p ∤ N: T_p^† = (T_p)_* = ⟨p⟩^{−1}T_p on V_ℓ, by Conrad's Theorem 5.8 (from the analytic Corollary 5.3 via the comparison of Weil pairing and cup product, Lemma 5.7).

w_ζ conjugates the (·)^*-action to the (·)_*-action. The source deduces this on V_ℓ(N) from the analytic Corollary 5.3 (w^*_ζ conjugates each T to its cup-product adjoint), Lemma 5.7 (cup product versus Weil pairing) and the faithfulness of the Tate-module functor. Since w_ζ is self-adjoint, [x, Ty] = [Tx, y].
Galois twist: g carries the moduli description of w_ζ to that of w_{g(ζ)}, since the Weil pairing is Galois-equivariant.
acceptance: On J₀(N) (trivial nebentypus), T_p (p ∤ N) is self-adjoint for the Weil pairing.
N = 11: every T ∈ T₁(11) = ℤ is self-adjoint.

nodes.title: The Tate module of J₁(N): a continuous G_ℚ-representation unramified outside Nℓ, commuting with T₁(N)
nodes.statement: T_ℓ(J₁(N)) = lim J₁(N)[ℓ^n](ℚ̄) ≅ T_ℓ(J₁(N)_ℂ) ≅ H¹(X₁(N)^an, ℤ) ⊗ ℤ_ℓ (for ℚ̄ ⊂ ℂ) carries a continuous action of G_ℚ, unramified at every p ∤ Nℓ, commuting with T₁(N) in either action. Hence ρ_{N,ℓ} : G_ℚ → Aut_{ℚ_ℓ⊗T₁(N)}(V_ℓ(N)) is a continuous representation, unramified outside Nℓ. Its target is GL₂(ℚ_ℓ ⊗ T₁(N)) once V_ℓ(N) is known to be free of rank 2 (ModularCurvesPartII:R14.3/betti-free-rank-two).
hypotheses: The comparison with H¹(X₁(N)^an, ℤ) depends on the choice of i = √−1; the intrinsic statement has 2πiℤ.
Unramifiedness is Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich: J₁(N) has good reduction at p ∤ N.
The actions commute because every T ∈ T₁(N) is defined over ℤ[1/N], hence over ℚ.
proofSteps: Galois action on T_ℓ: the ℓ-power torsion of an abelian variety over ℚ (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.6).
Unramified outside Nℓ: J₁(N) is an abelian scheme over ℤ[1/N] (node jacobian-and-functoriality) and Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich (R01.6).
Commutation: endomorphisms defined over ℚ commute with G_ℚ on ℚ̄-points.
acceptance: N = 11: V_ℓ(J₁(11)) is the Tate module of an elliptic curve isogenous to X₀(11), unramified outside 11ℓ.
The representation depends on the chosen action: through (·)^* or (·)_*, the characteristic polynomial of Frob_p differs by the nebentypus (Conrad Theorem 5.12, R14.6).
